conclusion: Same learned CMNET2 architecture/checkpoint family, different orchestration defaults. Replacing only the reference generator in our tested pipeline is not equivalent to running HAVC defaults.

comparison.havc: Same checkpoint; native PyTorch DINOv3 encoder
comparison.effect: Same intended learned weights; exact native/HF output parity was not measured in this audit.

comparison.havc: Auto selects medium for 16:9: 512×288 using Spline36; slow 640×360
comparison.effect: Default HAVC uses substantially fewer spatial tokens.

comparison.tested: All 87 curated FLUX anchors cached and available in every shot
comparison.havc: Default sliding window of 20 anchors, generated in pairs
comparison.effect: Reference availability changes as the film advances; distant costume views may leave the window.

comparison.tested: Fresh propagator for every detected shot
comparison.havc: Continuous propagator; scene flags select anchors, PermMemWindowDit slides memory
comparison.effect: Shot-boundary behavior differs beyond which model generates references.

comparison.tested: top_k=30; mem_every=5; deep_update_every=-1; proximity bias disabled; exact sparse readout
comparison.havc: Same top-k/update defaults and disabled proximity bias; dense upstream readout
comparison.effect: Local optimization was checked against dense CPU output; up to one RGB byte difference in prior validation.
Alternative implementations of the same local correlation, not removed attention.
Execution/transport difference; encode_mode is not a color-setting switch.

comparison.havc: retry_threshold=0.0 disables retry by default; optional new anchor and blended second pass
comparison.effect: Equivalent when disabled; enabling retry introduces additional coloring beyond initial references.

comparison.tested: Resize predicted Lab chroma, restore original Lab luminance; no saturation boost
comparison.havc: Spline36 upscale, recover source luma; render_vivid=False
comparison.effect: Same source-luminance objective; Lab reconstruction versus VapourSynth YUV chroma/luma is not byte-identical.

recommendation: Keep the user's approved CMNET2 render as the quality baseline. HAVC is an integrated automation route, not a new learned colorizer; preserve the tested reference bank/resolution/reset policy when isolating DiT reference quality.
